definitions.explanation: A water-filled ditch surrounding a castle or fortification.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}の{周|まわ}りに{堀|ほり}がある。
examples.english: There is a moat around the castle.

examples.japanese: {堀|ほり}に{鯉|こい}が{泳|およ}いでいる。
examples.english: Carp are swimming in the moat.

examples.japanese: {内堀|うちぼり}と{外堀|そとぼり}が{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: The inner and outer moats remain.

notes:
Commonly seen around Japanese castles and historical sites.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・{内堀|うちぼり} (inner moat)
・{外堀|そとぼり} (outer moat)
・{空堀|からぼり} (dry moat)
・{水堀|みずぼり} (water-filled moat)

FAMOUS EXAMPLES:
・{皇居|こうきょ}の{堀|ほり} (Imperial Palace moat in Tokyo)
・{大阪城|おおさかじょう}の{堀|ほり} (Osaka Castle moat)

IDIOM:
・{外堀|そとぼり}を{埋|う}める (to fill in the outer moat - to gradually corner someone or prepare the groundwork)
